publish.title: London burns, 1666: the Great Fire in 45 seconds
publish.description: How the fire started, how long it lasted, and how London was rebuilt.

scenes.headline: London burns, 1666
scenes.narration: In September 1666, a fire in a baker's house grew into the biggest fire London had ever seen.

scenes.headline: Five days in September
scenes.narration: It began on Sunday the second of September in Pudding Lane. A violent east wind spread it through Monday and Tuesday, and by Thursday it was extinguished.

points.label: Sunday 2 Sept
points.text: A fire starts in the king's baker's house

points.label: Mon and Tue
points.text: A violent east wind spreads it

scenes.headline: One more flare-up
scenes.narration: Thursday evening the flames burst out again at the Temple. Some houses were blown up with gunpowder to stop the spread.

scenes.headline: The damage
scenes.narration: About thirteen thousand houses burned, along with eighty-seven parish churches and old Saint Paul's Cathedral.

scenes.headline: The old streets returned
scenes.narration: Christopher Wren, John Evelyn and Robert Hooke each offered plans to redesign the city. None was adopted, and the old street lines mostly came back.

scenes.headline: Find the Monument
scenes.narration: The Monument near London Bridge stands close to where the fire began.
